title: [VOQ] system neigh was not installed in kernel
author: ysmanman

#### Description

<!--
     Briefly describe the problem you are having in a few paragraphs.
-->

We observed that a system neigh was not installed in kernel on some remote LC when triaging voq test failure in T2 testing. This was seen with internal build of 202205 image.

Our chassis for T2 testing has 3 LCs: `cmp227-4`, `cmp227-5`, `cmp227-6`. The neigh in question is `10.0.0.157`, which was bgp peer of PortChannel1058 on cmp227-6.  
```
admin@cmp227-6:~$ show ip interfaces | grep 10.0.0.157
PortChannel1058            10.0.0.156/31        up/up         ARISTA50T1      10.0.0.157
admin@cmp227-6:~$
```
The neighbor was added in chassis_db:
```
admin@cmp227-6:~$ sonic-db-cli CHASSIS_APP_DB hgetall "SYSTEM_NEIGH|cmp227-6|Asic0|PortChannel1058|10.0.0.157"
{'encap_index': '1074790409', 'neigh': '12:50:48:6a:41:16'}
admin@cmp227-6:~$
```
The neighbor was installed in kernel on `cmp227-4`:
```
admin@cmp227-4:~$ sudo ip netns exec asic0 ip neigh show 10.0.0.157  
10.0.0.157 dev Ethernet-IB0 lladdr 94:8e:d3:5e:85:04 PERMANENT
admin@cmp227-4:~$ sudo ip netns exec asic0 ip route show 10.0.0.157/32    
10.0.0.157 dev Ethernet-IB0 scope link 
admin@cmp227-4:~$ 
```
But it was not installed on `cmp227-5`:
```
admin@cmp227-5:~$ ip neigh show 10.0.0.157
10.0.0.157 dev Ethernet-IB0  FAILED
admin@cmp227-5:~$ ip route show 10.0.0.157/32
admin@cmp227-5:~$ 
```

comments.author: ysmanman
comments.body:
According to swss rec,  the latest updates  on the system neigh from chassis_db were: 
```
admin@cmp227-5:~$ sudo grep -a 10.0.0.157 /var/log/swss/swss.rec* | grep SYSTEM_NEIGH
/var/log/swss/swss.rec.1:2023-05-30.19:34:16.878385|SYSTEM_NEIGH|cmp227-6|Asic0|PortChannel1058|10.0.0.157|SET|encap_index:1074790425|neigh:12:50:48:6a:41:16
/var/log/swss/swss.rec.1:2023-05-30.19:38:28.652424|SYSTEM_NEIGH|cmp227-6|Asic0|PortChannel1058|10.0.0.157|DEL
/var/log/swss/swss.rec.1:2023-05-30.19:38:28.652439|SYSTEM_NEIGH|cmp227-6|Asic0|PortChannel1058|10.0.0.157|SET|encap_index:1074790409|neigh:12:50:48:6a:41:16
admin@cmp227-5:~$
```
The last update on the neighbor was `SET`. However, according to syslog, the last even  was to delete the neighbor from kernel, which was for `DEL` update sent before `SET`. 
```
admin@cmp227-5:~$ sudo grep -a 10.0.0.157 /var/log/syslog | grep Kernel
May 30 19:34:17.246507 cmp227-5 NOTICE swss#nbrmgrd: :- addKernelNeigh: IPv4 Nbr Add cmd: /sbin/ip neigh add 10.0.0.157 lladdr d4:af:f7:2e:c4:c6 dev Ethernet-IB0
May 30 19:34:17.250436 cmp227-5 NOTICE swss#nbrmgrd: :- addKernelRoute: IPv4 Route Add cmd: /sbin/ip route add 10.0.0.157/32 dev Ethernet-IB0
May 30 19:38:29.831266 cmp227-5 NOTICE swss#nbrmgrd: :- delKernelRoute: IPv4 Route Del cmd: /sbin/ip route del 10.0.0.157/32
May 30 19:38:29.832703 cmp227-5 NOTICE swss#nbrmgrd: :- delKernelNeigh: IPv4 Nbr Del cmd: /sbin/ip neigh del 10.0.0.157 dev Ethernet-IB0
admin@cmp227-5:~$
```

comments.author: ysmanman
comments.body:
I had a theory of the issue. The problematic sequence of system neighbor update is `SET`->`DEL`->`SET`.  So if the `DEL` & the 2nd `SET` update come in very close, it's possible that the `DEL` and the 2nd `SET` update can be *reordered*  due to race condition.

Detailedly, so cmp227-5 sees the following neighbor updates from chassis_db: 
```
/var/log/swss/swss.rec.1:2023-05-30.19:34:16.878385|SYSTEM_NEIGH|cmp227-6|Asic0|PortChannel1058|10.0.0.157|SET|encap_index:1074790425|neigh:12:50:48:6a:41:16
/var/log/swss/swss.rec.1:2023-05-30.19:38:28.652424|SYSTEM_NEIGH|cmp227-6|Asic0|PortChannel1058|10.0.0.157|DEL
/var/log/swss/swss.rec.1:2023-05-30.19:38:28.652439|SYSTEM_NEIGH|cmp227-6|Asic0|PortChannel1058|10.0.0.157|SET|encap_index:1074790409|neigh:12:50:48:6a:41:16
```
The first `SET` update was processed successfully.  In the process of the subsequent `DEL` update,  `removeNeghbor` can return `false` if the nexthop is still used by routes:

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-swss/blob/4d9fb93c00e6e2d8ec590928da78f90931c6a85d/orchagent/neighorch.cpp#L1066-L1071

If `removeNeighbor` returns `false`, orchagent will retry `DEL` later. So if the `DEL` and the 2nd `SET` update come in very close, the retry could result in updates like `DEL (failed)` -> `SET` -> `DEL(retry and succeed)`, which mistakenly deletes neigh from kernel.
 
As an evidence of the above theory,  we observed the following log that indicates that the above two `SET` updates were processed consecutively, just like the change of encapIndex, because of retry of `DEL` update: 
```
May 30 19:38:28.681287 cmp227-5 NOTICE swss#orchagent: :- updateVoqNeighborEncapIndex: Updated voq encap index for neighbor 10.0.0.157 on cmp227-6|Asic0|PortChannel1058
May 30 19:38:28.681287 cmp227-5 NOTICE swss#orchagent: :- doVoqSystemNeighTask: VOQ encap index updated for neighbor cmp227-6|Asic0|PortChannel1058|10.0.0.157
```

linkedPullRequests.title: Remove system neigh DEL operation if SET operation succeeds
linkedPullRequests.author: ysmanman
linkedPullRequests.body:

4. Make sure your pull request adds related reviewers, asignees, labels

Please also provide the following information in this pull request:
-->

**What I did**
Remove system neighbor DEL operation in m_toSync if SET operation for the same neighbor succeeds. This is to avoid mistakenly removing the system neighbor.

**Why I did it**
Fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/15266

**How I verified it**
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/15266 was uncovered by https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/master/tests/voq/test_voq_disrupts.py.  The issue was not seen in the test anymore with the fix.

**Details if related**
